blocks.text:
# SM kicker — a tiny watchdog (two jobs, seconds each, ~zero runner cost).
#
# Canonical home for the SM-kicker watchdog every factory repo points at.
# The calling repo keeps a thin stub workflow that calls this one with the
# repo-specific names (defaults match flutter_agent_harness).
#
# Why it exists: a repo whose CI is dispatch-only (no `on.push` on PR
# heads) and whose Machine SM is the sole trigger has two gaps that leave
# a PR BLOCKED forever with zero required-check contexts on its head:
#
#   1. SM dead: the cron tick missed/failed and nothing re-arms it.
#      Fix: if no SM run is queued/running/in-progress — dispatch one tick.
#
#   2. Head completeness: pushes WITHOUT code changes (pure main-merge
#      commits — the SM's own silent update-branch, or a manual
#      "merge main into branch") fire no workflows by design, yet strict
#      `up-to-date` protection demands FRESH required checks on the new
#      head SHA. Fix: if a PR head is a codeless merge commit (2 parents,
#      0 files vs first parent) and carries NEITHER of the required check
#      contexts NOR an active CI run — dispatch the CI workflow on it.
#
# Code-bearing pushes (dev/rework/WIP) are deliberately NOT touched here:
# their validation schedule stays owned by the SM ("intermediate pushes
# are free"). The schedule leg re-checks open PRs every 30 min to also
# cover bot pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN (those fire no events at all).

name: Factory SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the Machine SM workflow in the caller repo'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the validation CI workflow to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:
        description: 'Workflow display NAME as it appears in the runs API'
        type: string
        default: 'CI'
      required_contexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check context names'
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'SM workflow file'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'CI workflow file to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:
        description: 'CI workflow display name'
        type: string
        default: 'CI'
      required_contexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check contexts'
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'

permissions:
  actions: write        # workflow_dispatch: sm / ci
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # Global group, but NO cancel-in-progress (fa #911 diagnosis,
  # 2026-09-25): a push on ANY PR branch used to kill the in-flight kicker
  # for every other branch, leaving sm-liveness/head-completeness
  # check-runs stamped CANCELLED on random heads and polluting PR check
  # rolls repo-wide. The kicker jobs are seconds-cheap watchdogs — let
  # them queue instead of cancelling; a bounded backlog is harmless.
  group: factory-sm-kicker
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
  SM_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.sm_workflow || 'machine-sm.yml' }}
  CI_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.ci_workflow || 'ci.yml' }}
  CI_DISPLAY: ${{ inputs.ci_display_name || 'CI' }}
  REQUIRED_CONTEXTS: ${{ inputs.required_contexts || 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate' }}

jobs:
  sm-liveness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch an SM tick if none is queued or running
        run: |
          active=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/workflows/$SM_WORKFLOW/runs?per_page=1" \
            --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending")] | length')
          if [ "${active:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "SM alive ($active active run(s)) — nothing to do"
          else
            echo "SM idle — dispatching a tick"
            # Real tick, always: the workflow_dispatch default is dryRun=true
            # (a safety default for HUMAN dispatches). A bare dispatch from the
            # kicker lands dry and cannot merge anything — live evidence
            # 2026-10-03: dart kicker fired within 7s of #340's checks but the
            # SM ran "(dry)" (runs 37152253853, 37157212391); every merge that
            # night rode manual -F dryRun=false ticks instead.
            gh workflow run "$SM_WORKFLOW" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" -F dryRun=false
          fi

  head-completeness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch CI on codeless PR heads that carry no required contexts
        run: |
          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = "push" ]; then
            if [ "$GITHUB_REF_TYPE" != "branch" ]; then echo "tag push — skip"; exit 0; fi
            branches=("${GITHUB_REF_NAME}")
          else
            mapfile -t branches < <(gh pr list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName')
            echo "scanning ${#branches[@]} open PR branch(es)"
          fi
          IFS=',' read -ra contexts <<< "$REQUIRED_CONTEXTS"
          jq_ctx=$(printf '%s\n' "${contexts[@]}" | jq -R . | jq -s .)
          for b in "${branches[@]}"; do
            sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$b" --jq .sha 2>/dev/null) || { echo "$b: no head, skip"; continue; }
            read -r parents files < <(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha" --jq '"\(.parents | length) \(.files | length)"')
            if [ "$parents" != "2" ] || [ "${files:-1}" != "0" ]; then
              echo "$b: code-bearing head — SM owns validation, skip"
              continue
            fi
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq --arg name "$CI_DISPLAY" '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == $name and (.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending"))] | length')
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI already active on ${sha:0:9} — skip"
              continue
            fi
            found=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha/check-runs?per_page=100" \
              --jq --argjson ctx "$jq_ctx" '[.check_runs[].name | select(. as $n | $ctx | index($n))] | length')
            if [ "${found:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: ${sha:0:9} already has required contexts — skip"
              continue
            fi
            # grace re-check: a CI dispatch may be in flight from the SM/chain
            sleep 45
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq --arg name "$CI_DISPLAY" '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == $name)] | length')
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI appeared during grace window — skip"
              continue
            fi
            echo "$b: codeless head ${sha:0:9} with zero required contexts — dispatching CI"
            gh workflow run "$CI_WORKFLOW" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --ref "$b"
          done

# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# Same freeze contract as dmtools-dart's machine-sm.yml: the workflow is
# pinned to an immutable SHA; agent code and the dmtools CLI resolve from
# RELEASES at run time via this repo's variables:
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
# Bump a version = repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
# NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm` group.

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@e611e5f4240e9c8a5cdbf10721562eb04513d006
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine login rides the
      # deployment-level input (#687), exactly like the factory's contract.
      machine-author: ai-teammate
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Factory-state snapshot → factory-data branch (board: site/factory,
      # third tab; fa machine-sm.yml parity — transport lives in
      # js/factoryState.js, publishing is opt-in per factory).
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"agents-state.json"}'
      # Silent branch updates: input channel (github.token via secrets/in
      # blocks arrives empty through a reusable call — live-verified).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

One subtle thing to note: `github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false'` — for workflow_dispatch input of type boolean, `github.event.inputs.dryRun` is a string 'true'/'false'. When dispatched via `-F dryRun=false`, the string is 'false', which is truthy in a JS-like `||` context! Wait — in GitHub Actions expressions, `||` treats non-empty strings as truthy. The string `'false'` is a NON-EMPTY string → truthy! So `github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false'` evaluates to `'false'` (the string) either way. Then `dryRun: 'false'` — string 'false' passed to a boolean-typed input of the reusable workflow... GitHub coerces the string 'false' to boolean false for typed inputs. instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `instruction…

blocks.text:
# SM kicker — a tiny watchdog (two jobs, seconds each, ~zero runner cost).
#
# Canonical home for the SM-kicker watchdog every factory repo points at.
# The calling repo keeps a thin stub workflow that calls this one with the
# repo-specific names (defaults match flutter_agent_harness).
#
# Why it exists: a repo whose CI is dispatch-only (no `on.push` on PR
# heads) and whose Machine SM is the sole trigger has two gaps that leave
# a PR BLOCKED forever with zero required-check contexts on its head:
#
#   1. SM dead: the cron tick missed/failed and nothing re-arms it.
#      Fix: if no SM run is queued/running/in-progress — dispatch one tick.
#
#   2. Head completeness: pushes WITHOUT code changes (pure main-merge
#      commits — the SM's own silent update-branch, or a manual
#      "merge main into branch") fire no workflows by design, yet strict
#      `up-to-date` protection demands FRESH required checks on the new
#      head SHA. Fix: if a PR head is a codeless merge commit (2 parents,
#      0 files vs first parent) and carries NEITHER of the required check
#      contexts NOR an active CI run — dispatch the CI workflow on it.
#
# Code-bearing pushes (dev/rework/WIP) are deliberately NOT touched here:
# their validation schedule stays owned by the SM ("intermediate pushes
# are free"). The schedule leg re-checks open PRs every 30 min to also
# cover bot pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN (those fire no events at all).

name: Factory SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the Machine SM workflow in the caller repo'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the validation CI workflow to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:
        description: 'Workflow display NAME as it appears in the runs API'
        type: string
        default: 'CI'
      required_contexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check context names'
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'SM workflow file'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'CI workflow file to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:
        description: 'CI workflow display name'
        type: string
        default: 'CI'
      required_contexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check contexts'
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'

permissions:
  actions: write        # workflow_dispatch: sm / ci
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # Global group, but NO cancel-in-progress (fa #911 diagnosis,
  # 2026-09-25): a push on ANY PR branch used to kill the in-flight kicker
  # for every other branch, leaving sm-liveness/head-completeness
  # check-runs stamped CANCELLED on random heads and polluting PR check
  # rolls repo-wide. The kicker jobs are seconds-cheap watchdogs — let
  # them queue instead of cancelling; a bounded backlog is harmless.
  group: factory-sm-kicker
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
  SM_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.sm_workflow || 'machine-sm.yml' }}
  CI_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.ci_workflow || 'ci.yml' }}
  CI_DISPLAY: ${{ inputs.ci_display_name || 'CI' }}
  REQUIRED_CONTEXTS: ${{ inputs.required_contexts || 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate' }}

jobs:
  sm-liveness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch an SM tick if none is queued or running
        run: |
          active=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/workflows/$SM_WORKFLOW/runs?per_page=1" \
            --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending")] | length')
          if [ "${active:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "SM alive ($active active run(s)) — nothing to do"
          else
            echo "SM idle — dispatching a tick"
            # Real tick, always: the workflow_dispatch default is dryRun=true
            # (a safety default for HUMAN dispatches). A bare dispatch from the
            # kicker lands dry and cannot merge anything — live evidence
            # 2026-10-03: dart kicker fired within 7s of #340's checks but the
            # SM ran "(dry)" (runs 37152253853, 37157212391); every merge that
            # night rode manual -F dryRun=false ticks instead.
            gh workflow run "$SM_WORKFLOW" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" -F dryRun=false
          fi

  head-completeness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch CI on codeless PR heads that carry no required contexts
        run: |
          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = "push" ]; then
            if [ "$GITHUB_REF_TYPE" != "branch" ]; then echo "tag push — skip"; exit 0; fi
            branches=("${GITHUB_REF_NAME}")
          else
            mapfile -t branches < <(gh pr list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName')
            echo "scanning ${#branches[@]} open PR branch(es)"
          fi
          IFS=',' read -ra contexts <<< "$REQUIRED_CONTEXTS"
          jq_ctx=$(printf '%s\n' "${contexts[@]}" | jq -R . | jq -s .)
          for b in "${branches[@]}"; do
            sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$b" --jq .sha 2>/dev/null) || { echo "$b: no head, skip"; continue; }
            read -r parents files < <(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha" --jq '"\(.parents | length) \(.files | length)"')
            if [ "$parents" != "2" ] || [ "${files:-1}" != "0" ]; then
              echo "$b: code-bearing head — SM owns validation, skip"
              continue
            fi
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq --arg name "$CI_DISPLAY" '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == $name and (.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending"))] | length')
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI already active on ${sha:0:9} — skip"
              continue
            fi
            found=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha/check-runs?per_page=100" \
              --jq --argjson ctx "$jq_ctx" '[.check_runs[].name | select(. as $n | $ctx | index($n))] | length')
            if [ "${found:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: ${sha:0:9} already has required contexts — skip"
              continue
            fi
            # grace re-check: a CI dispatch may be in flight from the SM/chain
            sleep 45
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq --arg name "$CI_DISPLAY" '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == $name)] | length')
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI appeared during grace window — skip"
              continue
            fi
            echo "$b: codeless head ${sha:0:9} with zero required contexts — dispatching CI"
            gh workflow run "$CI_WORKFLOW" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --ref "$b"
          done

# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# Same freeze contract as dmtools-dart's machine-sm.yml: the workflow is
# pinned to an immutable SHA; agent code and the dmtools CLI resolve from
# RELEASES at run time via this repo's variables:
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
# Bump a version = repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
# NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm` group.

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@e611e5f4240e9c8a5cdbf10721562eb04513d006
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine login rides the
      # deployment-level input (#687), exactly like the factory's contract.
      machine-author: ai-teammate
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Factory-state snapshot → factory-data branch (board: site/factory,
      # third tab; fa machine-sm.yml parity — transport lives in
      # js/factoryState.js, publishing is opt-in per factory).
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"agents-state.json"}'
      # Silent branch updates: input channel (github.token via secrets/in
      # blocks arrives empty through a reusable call — live-verified).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

blocks.text:
# SM kicker — a tiny watchdog (two jobs, seconds each, ~zero runner cost).
#
# Canonical home for the SM-kicker watchdog every factory repo points at.
# The calling repo keeps a thin stub workflow that calls this one with the
# repo-specific names (defaults match flutter_agent_harness).
#
# Why it exists: a repo whose CI is dispatch-only (no `on.push` on PR
# heads) and whose Machine SM is the sole trigger has two gaps that leave
# a PR BLOCKED forever with zero required-check contexts on its head:
#
#   1. SM dead: the cron tick missed/failed and nothing re-arms it.
#      Fix: if no SM run is queued/running/in-progress — dispatch one tick.
#
#   2. Head completeness: pushes WITHOUT code changes (pure main-merge
#      commits — the SM's own silent update-branch, or a manual
#      "merge main into branch") fire no workflows by design, yet strict
#      `up-to-date` protection demands FRESH required checks on the new
#      head SHA. Fix: if a PR head is a codeless merge commit (2 parents,
#      0 files vs first parent) and carries NEITHER of the required check
#      contexts NOR an active CI run — dispatch the CI workflow on it.
#
# Code-bearing pushes (dev/rework/WIP) are deliberately NOT touched here:
# their validation schedule stays owned by the SM ("intermediate pushes
# are free"). The schedule leg re-checks open PRs every 30 min to also
# cover bot pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN (those fire no events at all).

name: Factory SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the Machine SM workflow in the caller repo'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the validation CI workflow to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:
        description: 'Workflow display NAME as it appears in the runs API'
        type: string
        default: 'CI'
      required_contexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check context names'
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'SM workflow file'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'CI workflow file to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:
        description: 'CI workflow display name'
        type: string
        default: 'CI'
      required_contexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check contexts'
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'

permissions:
  actions: write        # workflow_dispatch: sm / ci
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # Global group, but NO cancel-in-progress (fa #911 diagnosis,
  # 2026-09-25): a push on ANY PR branch used to kill the in-flight kicker
  # for every other branch, leaving sm-liveness/head-completeness
  # check-runs stamped CANCELLED on random heads and polluting PR check
  # rolls repo-wide. The kicker jobs are seconds-cheap watchdogs — let
  # them queue instead of cancelling; a bounded backlog is harmless.
  group: factory-sm-kicker
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
  SM_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.sm_workflow || 'machine-sm.yml' }}
  CI_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.ci_workflow || 'ci.yml' }}
  CI_DISPLAY: ${{ inputs.ci_display_name || 'CI' }}
  REQUIRED_CONTEXTS: ${{ inputs.required_contexts || 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate' }}

jobs:
  sm-liveness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch an SM tick if none is queued or running
        run: |
          active=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/workflows/$SM_WORKFLOW/runs?per_page=1" \
            --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending")] | length')
          if [ "${active:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "SM alive ($active active run(s)) — nothing to do"
          else
            echo "SM idle — dispatching a tick"
            # Real tick, always: the workflow_dispatch default is dryRun=true
            # (a safety default for HUMAN dispatches). A bare dispatch from the
            # kicker lands dry and cannot merge anything — live evidence
            # 2026-10-03: dart kicker fired within 7s of #340's checks but the
            # SM ran "(dry)" (runs 37152253853, 37157212391); every merge that
            # night rode manual -F dryRun=false ticks instead.
            gh workflow run "$SM_WORKFLOW" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" -F dryRun=false
          fi

  head-completeness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch CI on codeless PR heads that carry no required contexts
        run: |
          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = "push" ]; then
            if [ "$GITHUB_REF_TYPE" != "branch" ]; then echo "tag push — skip"; exit 0; fi
            branches=("${GITHUB_REF_NAME}")
          else
            mapfile -t branches < <(gh pr list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName')
            echo "scanning ${#branches[@]} open PR branch(es)"
          fi
          IFS=',' read -ra contexts <<< "$REQUIRED_CONTEXTS"
          jq_ctx=$(printf '%s\n' "${contexts[@]}" | jq -R . | jq -s .)
          for b in "${branches[@]}"; do
            sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$b" --jq .sha 2>/dev/null) || { echo "$b: no head, skip"; continue; }
            read -r parents files < <(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha" --jq '"\(.parents | length) \(.files | length)"')
            if [ "$parents" != "2" ] || [ "${files:-1}" != "0" ]; then
              echo "$b: code-bearing head — SM owns validation, skip"
              continue
            fi
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq --arg name "$CI_DISPLAY" '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == $name and (.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending"))] | length')
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI already active on ${sha:0:9} — skip"
              continue
            fi
            found=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha/check-runs?per_page=100" \
              --jq --argjson ctx "$jq_ctx" '[.check_runs[].name | select(. as $n | $ctx | index($n))] | length')
            if [ "${found:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: ${sha:0:9} already has required contexts — skip"
              continue
            fi
            # grace re-check: a CI dispatch may be in flight from the SM/chain
            sleep 45
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq --arg name "$CI_DISPLAY" '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == $name)] | length')
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI appeared during grace window — skip"
              continue
            fi
            echo "$b: codeless head ${sha:0:9} with zero required contexts — dispatching CI"
            gh workflow run "$CI_WORKFLOW" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --ref "$b"
          done

# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop

blocks.text:
# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# Same freeze contract as dmtools-dart's machine-sm.yml: the workflow is
# pinned to an immutable SHA; agent code and the dmtools CLI resolve from
# RELEASES at run time via this repo's variables:
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
# Bump a version = repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
# NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm` group.

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@e611e5f4240e9c8a5cdbf10721562eb04513d006
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine login rides the
      # deployment-level input (#687), exactly like the factory's contract.
      machine-author: ai-teammate
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Factory-state snapshot → factory-data branch (board: site/factory,
      # third tab; fa machine-sm.yml parity — transport lives in
      # js/factoryState.js, publishing is opt-in per factory).
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"agents-state.json"}'
      # Silent branch updates: input channel (github.token via secrets/in
      # blocks arrives empty through a reusable call — live-verified).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

One subtle thing to note: `github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false'` — for workflow_dispatch input of type boolean, `github.event.inputs.dryRun` is a string 'true'/'false'. When dispatched via `-F dryRun=false`, the string is 'false', which is truthy in a JS-like `||` context! Wait — in GitHub Actions expressions, `||` treats non-empty strings as truthy. The string `'false'` is a NON-EMPTY string → truthy! So `github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false'` evaluates to `'false'` (the string) either way. Then `dryRun: 'false'` — string 'false' passed to a boolean-typed input of the reusable workflow... GitHub coerces the string 'false' to boolean false for typed inputs. So `dryRun` = false → live run. 

And when dispatched with `-F dryRun=true`: input string is 'true' → truthy → 'true' → coerced to boolean true → dry run. So both paths work correctly. The `|| 'false'` fallback only matters when the input is absent (cron ticks, where `github.event.inputs.dryRun` is empty/null → falsy → 'false' → false → live). All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

blocks.text:
# SM kicker — a tiny watchdog (two jobs, seconds each, ~zero runner cost).
#
# Canonical home for the SM-kicker watchdog every factory repo points at.
# The calling repo keeps a thin stub workflow that calls this one with the
# repo-specific names (defaults match flutter_agent_harness).
#
# Why it exists: a repo whose CI is dispatch-only (no `on.push` on PR
# heads) and whose Machine SM is the sole trigger has two gaps that leave
# a PR BLOCKED forever with zero required-check contexts on its head:
#
#   1. SM dead: the cron tick missed/failed and nothing re-arms it.
#      Fix: if no SM run is queued/running/in-progress — dispatch one tick.
#
#   2. Head completeness: pushes WITHOUT code changes (pure main-merge
#      commits — the SM's own silent update-branch, or a manual
#      "merge main into branch") fire no workflows by design, yet strict
#      `up-to-date` protection demands FRESH required checks on the new
#      head SHA. Fix: if a PR head is a codeless merge commit (2 parents,
#      0 files vs first parent) and carries NEITHER of the required check
#      contexts NOR an active CI run — dispatch the CI workflow on it.
#
# Code-bearing pushes (dev/rework/WIP) are deliberately NOT touched here:
# their validation schedule stays owned by the SM ("intermediate pushes
# are free"). The schedule leg re-checks open PRs every 30 min to also
# cover bot pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN (those fire no events at all).

name: Factory SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the Machine SM workflow in the caller repo'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the validation CI workflow to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:
        description: 'Workflow display NAME as it appears in the runs API'
        type: string
        default: 'CI'
      required_contexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check context names'
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'SM workflow file'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'CI workflow file to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:
        description: 'CI workflow display name'
        type: string
        default: 'CI'
      required_contexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check contexts'
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'

permissions:
  actions: write        # workflow_dispatch: sm / ci
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # Global group, but NO cancel-in-progress (fa #911 diagnosis,
  # 2026-09-25): a push on ANY PR branch used to kill the in-flight kicker
  # for every other branch, leaving sm-liveness/head-completeness
  # check-runs stamped CANCELLED on random heads and polluting PR check
  # rolls repo-wide. The kicker jobs are seconds-cheap watchdogs — let
  # them queue instead of cancelling; a bounded backlog is harmless.
  group: factory-sm-kicker
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
  SM_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.sm_workflow || 'machine-sm.yml' }}
  CI_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.ci_workflow || 'ci.yml' }}
  CI_DISPLAY: ${{ inputs.ci_display_name || 'CI' }}
  REQUIRED_CONTEXTS: ${{ inputs.required_contexts || 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate' }}

jobs:
  sm-liveness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch an SM tick if none is queued or running
        run: |
          active=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/workflows/$SM_WORKFLOW/runs?per_page=1" \
            --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending")] | length')
          if [ "${active:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "SM alive ($active active run(s)) — nothing to do"
          else
            echo "SM idle — dispatching a tick"
            # Real tick, always: the workflow_dispatch default is dryRun=true
            # (a safety default for HUMAN dispatches). A bare dispatch from the
            # kicker lands dry and cannot merge anything — live evidence
            # 2026-10-03: dart kicker fired within 7s of #340's checks but the
            # SM ran "(dry)" (runs 37152253853, 37157212391); every merge that
            # night rode manual -F dryRun=false ticks instead.
            gh workflow run "$SM_WORKFLOW" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" -F dryRun=false
          fi

  head-completeness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch CI on codeless PR heads that carry no required contexts
        run: |
          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = "push" ]; then
            if [ "$GITHUB_REF_TYPE" != "branch" ]; then echo "tag push — skip"; exit 0; fi
            branches=("${GITHUB_REF_NAME}")
          else
            mapfile -t branches < <(gh pr list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName')
            echo "scanning ${#branches[@]} open PR branch(es)"
          fi
          IFS=',' read -ra contexts <<< "$REQUIRED_CONTEXTS"
          jq_ctx=$(printf '%s\n' "${contexts[@]}" | jq -R . | jq -s .)
          for b in "${branches[@]}"; do
            sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$b" --jq .sha 2>/dev/null) || { echo "$b: no head, skip"; continue; }
            read -r parents files < <(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha" --jq '"\(.parents | length) \(.files | length)"')
            if [ "$parents" != "2" ] || [ "${files:-1}" != "0" ]; then
              echo "$b: code-bearing head — SM owns validation, skip"
              continue
            fi
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq --arg name "$CI_DISPLAY" '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == $name and (.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending"))] | length')
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI already active on ${sha:0:9} — skip"
              continue
            fi
            found=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha/check-runs?per_page=100" \
              --jq --argjson ctx "$jq_ctx" '[.check_runs[].name | select(. as $n | $ctx | index($n))] | length')
            if [ "${found:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: ${sha:0:9} already has required contexts — skip"
              continue
            fi
            # grace re-check: a CI dispatch may be in flight from the SM/chain
            sleep 45
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq --arg name "$CI_DISPLAY" '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == $name)] | length')
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI appeared during grace window — skip"
              continue
            fi
            echo "$b: codeless head ${sha:0:9} with zero required contexts — dispatching CI"
            gh workflow run "$CI_WORKFLOW" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --ref "$b"
          done

# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# Same freeze contract as dmtools-dart's machine-sm.yml: the workflow is
# pinned to an immutable SHA; agent code and the dmtools CLI resolve from
# RELEASES at run time via this repo's variables:
#   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
#   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
# Bump a version = repo-settings edit, never a workflow edit.
# NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm` group.

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main
    # (the frozen machine-loop home; bump the SHA only together with the
    # matching loop change).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@e611e5f4240e9c8a5cdbf10721562eb04513d006
    with:
      # No .dmtools/config.js in this repo — the machine login rides the
      # deployment-level input (#687), exactly like the factory's contract.
      machine-author: ai-teammate
      # This repo dispatches no CI on PR heads (docs checks only) — the SM
      # leaves validation to the event-driven merge bot and labels.
      ci-workflow: ''
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # Factory-state snapshot → factory-data branch (board: site/factory,
      # third tab; fa machine-sm.yml parity — transport lives in
      # js/factoryState.js, publishing is opt-in per factory).
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"agents-state.json"}'
      # Silent branch updates: input channel (github.token via secrets/in
      # blocks arrives empty through a reusable call — live-verified).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8.
